area_corrections:
Verified with my own disassembly (r2 = 0x803FFD00 from __init_registers 0x80003280/84), a full r2-reader scan of the DOL text, and the decomp. Every Gecko line's vanilla and patched word, and every cave instruction, match the finder's decode. Corrections that cut across items:
(1) The finder calls the painter's two setOrtho sites and @5162/@5163 "the" shared 2D choke point, but that is incomplete. dOvlpFd2_dlst_c::draw (d_ovlp_fade2.cpp:102-104, bl setOrtho at 0x80223CF4) calls setOrtho(-9,-21,659,524) on the SHARED current graf port (r31 = *(0x803C4C08+0x5D00)) from its own constants @4024 0x803FB734 / @4026 0x803FB73C. The Gecko leaves these alone. Both of the finder's options (data rewrite or painter bl hooks) must also cover this site, or they are undone for the rest of that frame. gecko-not-covered wrongly calls it a "private uncompressed ortho". See missed item fade2-graf-reset.
(2) Several fixes proposed as "per-mode" rewrite instructions, not data: calcScissor 'li r3' at 0x8004A428, the lha->li at 0x801F0B70, the lfs-displacement patches, and the 3 'mr r4,r31'->'li r4,0' sites. A boot-time write in main01_init is fine. Switching live from T2/REL needs DCFlushRange + ICInvalidateRange on the word (CLAUDE.md gotcha #3, the JIT cache), or a hook_branchlink shim that reads the mode instead. Data words (.sdata2 floats, g_meterHIO / g_meter_mapHIO halfwords) have no such constraint.
(3) The constants the Gecko READS for its shift values are shared with unrelated code: @10325 0x803F92CC (114.0) is also read by dCamera_c::useItem0EvCamera 0x800BAAF4 and useItem1EvCamera 0x800BB5A4; @9542 0x803F8DAC (206) by drawPoison 0x800970E8; @5015 0x803F8B74 (320) by dKyr_lenzflare_move, dKyr_sun_move and dKyr_drawRain; @4390 0x803F85A4 (4/3) by dDemo_camera_c::JSGGetProjectionAspect 0x80069E34. @7214 0x803FB334 (320) has 8 readers in d_meter. Never rewrite these to carry our shift: put the shift in the mailbox, or in a cave or shim.
(4) The setUpRectangle side effect is not 'unknown': mDoGph_screenCapture is the Picto Box shutter. See the corrected gecko-setuprect-sideeffect, plus the new picto capture-rect item.
(5) The cave-collision correction to docs/design/widescreen-culling.md §9 stands. CanaryTRK = 0x8040CFB0..0x80410000 (wwapi/mailbox/mod.go:59,66). The DOLPatches file offsets map to exactly the finder's 12 addresses. No build.py hook site and no address literal in inject/rel or inject/include is within 0x10 of any Gecko site; the nearest is seachart_shim at 0x801BB06C (dDlst_FMAP_c::draw+0x48), clear of the Fmap patches at 0x801B6968/78/955C. Dolphin's installer is 0x80001800..0x80003000 (GeckoCode.h:46-47). The caves' vanilla bytes are all 0.
(6) Anchors marked "per the Gecko" (rupee counter and swim timer screens, keys, button cluster, place name) are unverified without the .blo files or a screenshot. Clean address verification does not upgrade them.

Each painter pair stores a TBox2 at r1+0x30 / r1+0x20, then does addi r4,r1,0x30|0x20 and bl setOrtho 0x802CDD14 at 0x8000B06C / 0x8000BA30, on the same J2DOrthoGraph at r1+0x118 (m_Do_graphic.cpp:1572-1573, 1890). setOrtho only stores mOrtho (J2DOrthoGraph.cpp:34-38), so a shim that edits *r4 before the tail-call works. The numbers check out: 659/889 x 4/3 = 0.988 (1.2% narrow); exact-F box -118.83..759.83. Missing piece: d_ovlp_fade2 resets the shared graf port's ortho from its own constants (missed item fade2-graf-reset), so the fix must also cover 0x80223CF4.

verdicts.notes: Cave D confirmed: TColor @4582 0x803F891C = 000000FF (opaque black). The calls are J2DFillBox(-130,-32,130,640) and (640,-32,130,640). J2DFillBox builds a local J2DOrthoGraph and never calls setPort (J2DOrthoGraph.cpp:73-77; fillBox only sets the blend mode and pos mtx), so the bars use whatever projection is current. That is the painter graf: dJle_Pb_c::draw ends with scrn1->draw(graph) then shutterLineDraw (no projection change), and dDlst_2DSCP_c::draw calls graf->setPort(). Both blr sites follow a complete epilogue, so the Gecko's tail branch is valid. The finder's proposed 'hook_branchlink tail hooks' cannot sit on a blr. The finder's WYSIWYG claim is wrong (see missed picto-capture-rect).

missed.what: The Picto Box photo capture is a fixed EFB rectangle that matches the vanilla viewfinder frame. Under global 2D compression the frame shrinks in EFB terms but the capture doesn't, and with the 3D widened the stored photo is anamorphic.
missed.where: m_Do_graphic.cpp:857-863 (mCaptureDraw=1, mCaptureSizeWidth=152, mCaptureSizeHeight=104, mCaptureCenterX=320, mCaptureCenterY=180); mDoGph_screenCapture :1466-1530 (GXSetTexCopySrc(centerX-sizeW, centerY-sizeH, 2*sizeW, 2*sizeH), half-res copy into a 152x104 texture); triggered from d_picture_box.cpp:661
missed.assumption: The viewfinder frame drawn in the 2D ortho covers the same EFB pixels (168..472 x 76..284) that are copied, and the 3D is drawn at 4:3, so the photo's pixel aspect is true.
missed.effect_native: In mode 2 (and under the Gecko) the compressed viewfinder frame covers only about EFB 206..435 (Gecko: 209..428), while the copy still takes EFB 168..472. Photos contain about F times more width than the frame shows (not WYSIWYG), and the texture is anamorphic. The album (with pictureDraw squeezed) then shows widescreen-taken photos 0.75x narrow, and the shutter preview is wrong under the Gecko's data rewrite. Photos are saved to the memory card, so the choice also affects how they look later in 4:3 mode.
missed.fix: A product decision. A GX EFB copy can only scale 1:1 or 2:1 in both axes, so no single-word fix exists. Option 1: while the Picto Box viewfinder is up (or only on the capture frame), drop the 3D aspect back to 4:3 (g_HIO.mAspectRatio or the culling block). The photo is then non-anamorphic and framed like vanilla, at the cost of a stretched scene while aiming (or a 1-frame glitch). Option 2: leave the viewfinder frame uncompressed in Picto mode so the frame matches the copy, keep photos anamorphic, and draw them with the full 640 viewport in pictureDraw.
